To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the levels of mRNA in post-mortem human brain are significantly influenced by gender, brain pH, and age at death.

the amounts of mRNA in post mortem human brain are influenced by the following factors: gender (mRNA levels in females are lower than in males), age at death (in control brains mRNA levels decrease with increasing age), brain pH (higher pH values correspond to lower mRNA levels), agonal state (the agonal state does not influence mRNA levels) and inter-lobe variance (mRNA levels do not vary between different brain lobes).
the amounts of mRNA in post-mortem brain tissue are affected by age, gender, pH and post-mortem interval.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of gender, age, postmortem delay and brain pH on gene expression in post-mortem human brain.
the quantification of mRNA from postmortem human tissue, and how this can be influenced by a number of factors.
the effects of postmortem variables on mRNA expression in human brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gender and brain pH have the most significant effect upon mRNA levels in human brain, followed by age at death.
the amount of mRNA measured in a postmortem brain sample is influenced by gender, age at time of death, brain pH, and postmortem interval.

gender, age at time of death, postmorten interval, brain pH and agonal state are all factors that can influence the amount of mRNA in post mortem brain samples and should be taken into account in the analysis of gene expression in human brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

gender is a significant variable, age at death is a poor predictor of gene expression, brain pH is a significant predictor of mRNA levels and postmortem interval is a significant variable in the AD brain.
mRNA quantification in human brain is influenced by gender, age at the time of death, brain pH and postmortem interval.

the effects of brain pH, gender, age, agonal state, inter-lobe variance, postmortem time and disease on the mRNA levels are not as strong as previously thought and that the effects of gender and brain pH should be considered in future work.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amount of RNA in a sample is influenced by a number of factors.
gender, age, brain pH and agonal state are all factors which should be taken into account in the analysis and interpretation of gene expression in the human brain.
gender, age, and brain pH should be taken into account as factors when quantifying gene levels in postmortem brains.
